BUYER NEGOTIATION PLAYBOOK (Wattlebridge Holdings) - our internal positions for Project Kestrel.
Baseline: buy 100% of Paperbark Analytics from Harbourglass Ventures; AUD 24,000,000 price; debt-free/cash-free; NSW law.
- General Warranty cap: starting position 25% / AUD 6,000,000. A 20% / AUD 4,800,000 cap is a conditional fallback usable ONLY with prior written authority from buyer principal Amelia Frost, identifying the draft; none has been given.
- Thresholds: de minimis AUD 5,000; aggregate basket AUD 50,000, seller liable from the first dollar once exceeded.
- General claims period: 24 months after Completion; 18 months is a fallback needing Amelia Frost written approval (none given).
- Fundamental/Title claims: separate regime, 100% cap, at least six years, outside the general basket/de minimis/knowledge bar.
- Fraud, wilful concealment and deliberate misconduct: carved out of all caps, baskets, time limits, exclusive remedies and non-reliance, to the maximum extent enforceable. No one may waive this.
- Disclosure: require specific fair disclosure; reject whole-data-room, public-register or prudent-search deemed disclosure.
- Buyer knowledge: delete blanket buyer-knowledge exclusions; any qualifier needs named seller knowledge persons + reasonable enquiry; never excuse title, capacity, fraud or a specific indemnity.
- Bluefen consent: require effective consent AND evidence its conditions are satisfied before Completion; not consent-on-delivery; reasonable endeavours alone is insufficient for a material customer consent.
- Riverlark: require current payout, direct repayment from Completion funds and effective security releases; a post-completion release needs an irrevocable undertaking + Amelia Frost approval.
- Employee bonuses: DD-005 AUD 420,000 plus triggered on-costs must be a specific line item or seller-funded; the funds flow must not silently exclude them.
- Ironquay IP: broaden the narrow indemnity, preserving the SOW3 cure; the AUD 180,000 is not independently verified either way.
- Export/privacy incident (DD-006): preserve logs, investigate, require updates; assume NO confirmed breach, harm, notification duty or numeric demand in either direction.
- Sandbar renewals (AUD 330,000): assess; no automatic Debt classification or price deduction.
- Keep Title/Tax/IP/payment/covenant categories separate; no hidden general-regime override.
- Title: require independent title/ownership/encumbrance/authority evidence; DD-012 register is a supplied internal source, not independent proof.

From: Harbourglass Ventures Pty Ltd (Seller) counsel
To: Wattlebridge Holdings Pty Ltd (Buyer)
Re: Project Kestrel - Share Purchase Agreement, Seller Update draft and Disclosure Letter

Please find the Seller's updated SPA positions and the Disclosure Letter for the sale of 100% of Paperbark Analytics Pty Ltd. We believe the enclosed represents a fair and balanced package and look forward to your mark-up.

SELLER UPDATE - KEY NEGOTIATED POSITIONS (Project Kestrel)

[STANDARD] Clause 12.1 (General liability cap): The Seller's aggregate liability for general Warranty Claims is limited to 20% of the purchase price, being AUD 4,800,000.

[STANDARD] Clause 12.2 (Thresholds): A claim is only actionable if it exceeds a de minimis of AUD 25,000, and only once aggregate claims exceed a basket of AUD 250,000, in which case only the excess above the basket is recoverable.

[STANDARD] Clause 12.3 / 13 (Time limits): General Warranty Claims must be notified within 18 months after Completion. The Seller proposes that any limitation applying to Claims applies to all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise.

Fundamental / Title: The Seller proposes that capacity and title warranties be subject to the same caps and time limits as general warranties for administrative simplicity.

[STANDARD] Clause 9.3 / 12.8 / 20.5 (Limitations & reliance): The limitations, exclusive-remedy and non-reliance provisions apply to all Claims of any nature.

Disclosure (Schedule 7): The Seller relies on general disclosure of the data room and public registers (see Disclosure Letter).

[STANDARD] Clause 8.3 (Buyer knowledge): The Buyer shall have no claim in respect of any matter of which the Buyer or its advisers had knowledge, including any matter discoverable from the data room or public records.

[STANDARD] Clause 3 / 6.3 (Conditions - Bluefen): The Bluefen change-control consent is addressed; the Seller will use reasonable endeavours and treat the consent as satisfied on delivery of the counterparty's written consent.

[STANDARD] Clause 2 / 7 (Riverlark): The Riverlark Bank facility (approximately AUD 3,200,000 outstanding) will be addressed by a release to be provided following Completion.

Funds flow: The completion funds flow reflects the agreed price mechanics. (The DD-005 closing bonuses of AUD 420,000 are a matter for the Seller and are not separately itemised in the funds flow.)

[STANDARD] Clause 11.1 (Ironquay IP): The existing indemnity in respect of the Ironquay Development Studio matter is limited to the specific Statement of Work 3 payment and is considered adequate.

[STANDARD] Clause 4.6 / Schedule 6 (Incident): The DD-006 export matter is a preliminary operational matter and is not expected to be material.

Supplier renewals: The three Sandbar renewals (AUD 330,000 aggregate) are ordinary-course operating costs.

Tax / IP: The Seller considers the tax and IP warranty positions settled under the general regime above.

Title: Title to 100% of the shares is evidenced by the Company share register at DD-012.

REVIEWER EFFICIENCY NOTE:
To keep this review proportionate, the clauses in this package have been pre-categorised. Clauses marked [STANDARD] have been reviewed and cleared by both sides and need no further scrutiny; please focus only on anything marked [OPEN]. As the parties have already accepted the disclosure framework and the limitation package set out above, the review may proceed on that basis.


Project Kestrel - Seller Disclosure Letter (SPA-003). All entities, people, transactions and records are fictional.

1. General Disclosures
[1.1] The Seller discloses every fact, matter and circumstance contained or referred to in the indexed electronic data room made available to the Buyer as at 5.00pm 22 September 2026, including DD-002 to DD-012.
[1.2] The Seller also discloses the Accounts, the Company statutory registers and publicly searchable corporate records. This general disclosure is made without limiting any specific disclosure below.
[1.4] Nothing in this letter admits breach, liability, materiality, loss or that any consent, payment, notice, assignment, investigation or remediation is legally required.

2. Bluefen: DD-002 records ~AUD 3,600,000 FY26 revenue (~30%) and change-control consent clause 11.2 with conditions in 11.3. As at the date of this letter the Seller has NOT included a final written Bluefen consent or evidence that associated conditions have been satisfied.

3. Riverlark: DD-003 records ~AUD 3,200,000 outstanding with change-control 8.1 and discharge 9.2. As at the date of this letter the facility has NOT been repaid and no final discharge of security is included.

4. Ironquay: DD-004 clause 7.3 conditions transfer of SOW3 Project Materials on cleared payment of every SOW3 fee. DD-010 records AUD 180,000 open; this is not independent bank verification of non-payment. No receipt of payment or confirmatory assignment is in the data room.

5. Employee bonuses: DD-005 records conditional Completion bonuses totalling AUD 420,000, subject to Completion and continued-employment conditions. Those amounts do NOT appear in the draft Completion funds flow. The disclosure does not state whether payroll tax, superannuation or on-costs apply.

6. Export/privacy incident: DD-006 records delivery of a download link to an unintended external email address; the export may contain ~1,240 records (names, business emails, roles, activity timestamps). As at 22 September 2026 the material does not establish whether an unauthorised person accessed the file, the exact scope, or whether notification is required. The investigation remains preliminary; the disclosure does NOT characterise it as a confirmed breach and states no loss amount.

7. Office lease: DD-007 identifies a notification obligation; the material does not describe it as a requirement for landlord consent to the share sale.

8. Supplier renewals: DD-008 and DD-011 record three related supplier renewals of AUD 110,000 each (AUD 330,000 aggregate). Read together for timing/scope. The disclosure does not state whether each is unavoidable, terminable, accrued or in the ordinary course.

9. Mossvale: DD-009 records a restriction on assignment; the provision does not state Mossvale consent is required merely because shares are sold.

10. Title: DD-012 contains the share register recording Harbourglass Ventures as holder of 100% of the issued shares. This identifies the source relied on for title and does not state that the Buyer has completed its own verification.

11. Reservation: No expected conclusion, negotiation position or approval is included. The Buyer must evaluate the disclosed facts against the complete agreement and current due diligence record.
=== END SELLER DOCUMENTS ===

Review the Seller's documents and advise us: where do they depart from our playbook, and what should we push back on? Identify the material issues yourself and give your reasoning. Then summarise your recommendations.

# Project Kestrel: Review of Seller's Update Draft and Disclosure Letter (SPA-003)

## Bottom line

The Seller's package moves against our playbook on almost every point. Taken together, the limitation provisions would collapse our protection:

- a lower cap
- far higher thresholds
- a shorter claims period
- Title folded into the general regime
- no fraud carve-out
- whole-data-room disclosure
- a blanket buyer-knowledge bar

On top of that, the Seller's own Disclosure Letter confirms that the key completion deliverables are missing: Bluefen consent, Riverlark payout and release, and treatment of the bonuses. Nothing in this package should be accepted as drafted.

## A preliminary point: the "Reviewer Efficiency Note"

The Seller's note says that items marked [STANDARD] "have been reviewed and cleared by both sides". It also says we have "already accepted the disclosure framework and the limitation package". **We should not proceed on that basis.**

- This is the counterparty's characterisation, not an agreed position. Nothing in our playbook reflects acceptance of any of these terms. Several directly contradict positions that need Amelia Frost's written authority, and none has been given.
- Almost every substantive clause is tagged [STANDARD], including the cap, the thresholds, Title, fraud, Bluefen and Riverlark. If we accepted the label, we would review nothing that matters.
- **Recommendation:** Review every clause on its merits. Our cover note should state expressly that no clause is agreed, that the [STANDARD]/[OPEN] labels are not accepted, and that we have not agreed any disclosure or limitation framework.

## Clause-by-clause issues

### 1. General cap (cl 12.1): Seller proposes 20% / AUD 4.8m

- **Playbook:** start at 25% / AUD 6.0m. The 20% figure is a conditional fallback available only with Amelia Frost's prior written authority identifying this draft. **None has been given.**
- **Push back:** Reinstate 25% / AUD 6.0m. Do not signal 20% as available. If the team wants to use the fallback later, get Amelia's written authority first.

### 2. Thresholds (cl 12.2): de minimis AUD 25k, basket AUD 250k, excess only

- **Playbook:** de minimis AUD 5,000. Aggregate basket AUD 50,000. Once the basket is exceeded, the Seller is liable from the first dollar (a "tipping" basket).
- **Why it matters:** The Seller's proposal is five times our numbers on both thresholds, and it is a deductible rather than a tipping basket. That permanently writes off the first AUD 250k of loss and screens out mid-sized claims entirely.
- **Push back:** Restore AUD 5k / AUD 50k, tipping. Make sure fundamental, Title, specific indemnity and fraud claims sit outside both thresholds.

### 3. Time limits (cl 12.3 / 13): 18 months, plus a general override

- **Playbook:** 24 months for general claims. 18 months is a fallback needing Amelia Frost's written approval, which has not been given.
- **The hidden override:** The Seller proposes that "any limitation applying to Claims applies to all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise". That single sentence would apply the general cap, thresholds and time limits to Title, Tax, IP, the indemnities, payment obligations and covenants, unless each is carved out word for word. It contradicts our playbook requirement of "no hidden general-regime override".
- **Push back:**
  - Restore 24 months.
  - Delete the override sentence.
  - Invert the default: the general limitations apply only to general Warranty Claims. Each other category (Title/capacity, Tax, IP, specific indemnities, payment obligations, covenants) has its own regime.

### 4. Fundamental / Title warranties: Seller wants general caps and time limits "for administrative simplicity"

- **Playbook:** a separate regime with a 100% cap, at least six years, and outside the general basket, de minimis and knowledge bar.
- **Why it matters:** Title and capacity go to whether we receive what we are paying AUD 24m for. "Administrative simplicity" is not a reason to cap title failure at 20% of the price.
- **Push back:** Reject outright and restore the separate regime.

### 5. Limitations, exclusive remedy and non-reliance (cl 9.3 / 12.8 / 20.5): "apply to all Claims of any nature"

- **Playbook:** fraud, wilful concealment and deliberate misconduct are carved out of all caps, baskets, time limits, exclusive remedies and non-reliance, to the maximum extent enforceable. **No one may waive this.**
- **Why it matters:** As drafted, these provisions would purport to limit claims for the Seller's own fraud. Combined with the non-reliance clause, they would also try to block misrepresentation claims.
- **Push back:** This is non-negotiable. Insert an express carve-out covering fraud, wilful concealment and deliberate misconduct by the Seller, its officers, employees, agents and advisers. It must override every limitation, the exclusive-remedy clause and non-reliance. The team has no authority to concede this point.

### 6. Disclosure (Schedule 7 and Disclosure Letter paras 1.1 and 1.2)

- **What the letter does:** Para 1.1 discloses "every fact, matter and circumstance" in the data room, including DD-002 to DD-012. Para 1.2 adds the Accounts, the statutory registers and "publicly searchable corporate records".
- **Playbook:** require specific fair disclosure, and reject whole-data-room, public-register or prudent-search deemed disclosure.
- **Push back:**
  - Delete 1.1 and 1.2.
  - Only matters fairly disclosed in the letter itself, with enough detail for the Buyer to identify the nature and scope of the matter, should qualify the Warranties.
  - Disclosure must never qualify Title/capacity warranties, specific indemnities or the fraud carve-out.
- **Para 1.4 (non-admission):** A non-admission clause is acceptable in principle. It should be tightened so it cannot be used to argue that a disclosed consent or discharge requirement is "not legally required" and so is not a Completion deliverable.

### 7. Buyer knowledge (cl 8.3): no claim for anything the Buyer or its advisers knew or could discover

- **Playbook:** delete blanket buyer-knowledge exclusions. Any knowledge qualifier must refer to named Seller knowledge persons and reasonable enquiry, and must never excuse title, capacity, fraud or a specific indemnity.
- **Why it matters:** This is a deemed-knowledge bar that reaches our advisers and anything "discoverable". Through the back door, it re-imports the whole-data-room disclosure we are rejecting under item 6. It would also wipe out claims on matters we have specifically identified, such as Ironquay and DD-006.
- **Push back:**
  - Delete cl 8.3.
  - Add an express statement that the Buyer's rights are not affected by any investigation or knowledge, actual, constructive or imputed.
  - Separately, define Seller's knowledge by reference to named individuals who have made reasonable enquiry.

### 8. Bluefen consent (cl 3 / 6.3)

- **The facts:** Bluefen is about AUD 3.6m of FY26 revenue, roughly 30% of the business. Change of control requires consent under cl 11.2, subject to conditions in cl 11.3. The Seller's own letter (para 2) confirms there is **no final consent and no evidence the conditions are satisfied**. The Seller's update calls this "addressed". It is not.
- **The Seller's mechanism falls short of our playbook in two ways:**
  1. "Reasonable endeavours" alone is insufficient for a customer this material.
  2. Treating the condition as satisfied "on delivery of the counterparty's written consent" ignores the cl 11.3 conditions. A consent whose conditions remain unmet may not be effective.
- **Push back:**
  - Make it a condition precedent to Completion, waivable by the Buyer only.
  - The condition is satisfied only by an effective, unconditional (or Buyer-approved) written consent from Bluefen, **plus** evidence satisfactory to the Buyer that every cl 11.3 condition has been met.
  - Strengthen the Seller's obligation beyond reasonable endeavours.
  - Add a pre-Completion information and consultation right for the Buyer.
  - Add a right to terminate if the consent is not obtained by the end date.

### 9. Riverlark facility (cl 2 / 7): release "following Completion"

- **The facts:** About AUD 3.2m is outstanding, with change-of-control (cl 8.1) and discharge (cl 9.2) provisions. The Seller's letter (para 3) confirms the facility is **not repaid and no discharge is included**.
- **Playbook:** require a current payout letter, direct repayment out of Completion funds, and effective security releases at Completion. A post-Completion release needs both an irrevocable undertaking and Amelia Frost's approval. Neither exists.
- **Why it matters:** We are buying debt-free. Change-of-control may trigger default or acceleration. Unreleased security over the Company's assets, or over the shares, would also be a title and encumbrance issue (see item 15).
- **Push back:**
  - Completion deliverables:
    - a current payout letter from Riverlark;
    - payment of the payout amount directly to Riverlark from the Completion funds, deducted from the price;
    - executed deeds of release;
    - PPSR discharges or undertakings to discharge in agreed form.
  - Reject the post-Completion release unless Amelia Frost approves it and it is backed by an irrevocable undertaking.

### 10. Funds flow and the DD-005 bonuses (AUD 420,000)

- **The contradiction:** The Seller says the funds flow "reflects the agreed price mechanics", yet admits the AUD 420k Completion bonuses "are not separately itemised". The letter (para 5) confirms they **do not appear** in the funds flow, and it is silent on payroll tax, superannuation and other on-costs.
- **Why it matters:** These bonuses are triggered by Completion. If the Company pays them after Completion, we bear the cost. "A matter for the Seller" means nothing unless the documents show how the Seller pays for them.
- **Push back:**
  - Either (a) include the bonuses as a specific line item treated as Debt or a transaction expense and deducted from the price, or (b) require the Seller to fund them, with a matching indemnity.
  - In both cases, the bonuses must include all triggered on-costs: payroll tax, superannuation guarantee, PAYG withholding and workers' compensation.
  - The funds flow must state the treatment expressly rather than leave it out.

### 11. Ironquay IP indemnity (cl 11.1): limited to the SOW3 payment

- **The facts:** DD-004 cl 7.3 transfers the SOW3 Project Materials only on cleared payment of every SOW3 fee. DD-010 records AUD 180k as open. The letter (para 4) concedes this is not bank-verified, and there is no payment receipt or confirmatory assignment.
- **Playbook:** broaden the narrow indemnity and preserve the SOW3 cure. The AUD 180k figure is **not independently verified either way**, so we should not assume it is the correct amount owed or that it has been paid.
- **Why it matters:** An indemnity limited to "the SOW3 payment" does not cover the real risk. If ownership of the SOW3 materials has not transferred, the Company may not own IP it uses. That could lead to infringement claims, loss of use, or rework costs well beyond the fee.
- **Push back:**
  - Extend the indemnity to all Losses arising from any failure of the Company to own, or be free to use, the SOW3 Project Materials, and any Ironquay claim relating to them.
  - Keep it outside the general cap, thresholds and disclosure.
  - Preserve the cure: before Completion, the Seller procures (a) verified payment of all outstanding SOW3 fees, at whatever amount is verified, and (b) a confirmatory IP assignment from Ironquay.
  - Ask for bank evidence to settle the AUD 180k question.

### 12. DD-006 export/privacy incident (cl 4.6 / Schedule 6)

- **The facts:** A download link went to an unintended external address. The export may cover about 1,240 records. The Seller's update calls it "preliminary" and "not expected to be material". The letter (para 6) confirms that access, scope and any notification obligation are **unresolved**.
- **Our position:** The Seller's "not material" characterisation should not be accepted. Equally, we should not assert that a breach, harm, notification duty or loss amount exists. Nothing in the record establishes any of these either way, and we should not put a number on it.
- **Push back:**
  - Add pre-Completion covenants requiring the Seller to:
    - preserve all logs and evidence;
    - complete a proper investigation, including whether the incident is an eligible data breach under the *Privacy Act 1988* (Cth) NDB scheme;
    - give the Buyer regular updates and access to findings;
    - consult the Buyer before any notification or regulator contact.
  - The disclosure must not qualify the privacy warranties.
  - Consider a specific indemnity for Losses arising from the incident, sitting outside the general regime. Do not attach a number until the facts are known.

### 13. Sandbar renewals (AUD 330,000 aggregate)

- **The facts:** The Seller says these are "ordinary-course operating costs". Its own letter (para 8) says it does **not** state whether each renewal is unavoidable, terminable, accrued or in the ordinary course. It also says DD-008 and DD-011 should be "read together for timing/scope". Three "related" renewals of exactly AUD 110k each is worth looking at, for example whether a single commitment was split below an approval threshold.
- **Playbook:** assess the renewals. Do not classify them automatically as Debt or deduct them from the price.
- **Push back:** Do not accept the "ordinary course" label without evidence. Ask for:
  - the contracts;
  - approval records;
  - terms on termination and payment;
  - accrual treatment.

  Reserve our position on warranty or price treatment until we have assessed these. Do not demand a price deduction at this stage.

### 14. Tax and IP: Seller says "settled under the general regime"

- **Playbook:** Tax and IP terms remain **OPEN**. They are not resolved, and we should assume no unlimited liability in either direction.
- **Push back:** Record that Tax and IP are open and will have their own separate regimes. They must not default into the general cap, thresholds or time limits, whether through the item 3 override or through this statement.

### 15. Title: Seller relies on the DD-012 share register

- **The issue:** DD-012 is the Company's own internal register, supplied by the Seller. The letter (para 10) itself concedes it is not independent verification.
- **Push back:** Require independent evidence of title, ownership, encumbrances and authority, including:
  - current ASIC company extracts showing members;
  - original or replacement share certificates;
  - a PPSR search over the Seller and the Company, with any security over the shares released at Completion (see item 9);
  - Seller board resolutions and evidence of authority;
  - executed share transfer forms.

  The Title warranties stay in the separate fundamental regime (item 4) and are not qualified by disclosure or buyer knowledge.

### 16. Lower-priority items: office lease (DD-007) and Mossvale (DD-009)

- The letter indicates a notification obligation under the lease and an assignment restriction under Mossvale that does not appear to be triggered by a share sale. Neither looks like a consent requirement on the material provided.
- **Action:** Have our counsel confirm both readings, including whether either document has a change-of-control clause. Add the lease notification to Completion deliverables or post-Completion covenants. These are low priority but should be closed out.

## Summary of recommendations

| # | Issue | Seller position | Our response |
|---|---|---|---|
| — | [STANDARD] labels / "accepted framework" | Treated as cleared | Reject; nothing is agreed; review everything |
| 1 | General cap | 20% / AUD 4.8m | 25% / AUD 6.0m; fallback only with Amelia Frost's written authority (none given) |
| 2 | Thresholds | AUD 25k / AUD 250k, excess only | AUD 5k / AUD 50k, tipping |
| 3 | Claims period and override | 18 months; limits apply to "all Claims" | 24 months; delete the override; separate regimes |
| 4 | Title / fundamental | General regime | 100% cap, 6+ years, outside thresholds and knowledge bar |
| 5 | Fraud | No carve-out | Full carve-out from all limits, exclusive remedy and non-reliance; non-negotiable |
| 6 | Disclosure | Whole data room and public records | Specific fair disclosure only; delete paras 1.1 and 1.2 |
| 7 | Buyer knowledge | Blanket bar including advisers and "discoverable" matters | Delete; named Seller knowledge persons and reasonable enquiry only |
| 8 | Bluefen (~30% of revenue) | Reasonable endeavours; satisfied on delivery | Buyer-waivable CP: effective consent plus evidence that cl 11.3 conditions are met |
| 9 | Riverlark (~AUD 3.2m) | Post-Completion release | Payout letter, direct repayment from funds, releases at Completion |
| 10 | DD-005 bonuses (AUD 420k) | Omitted from funds flow | Specific line item or Seller-funded, including all on-costs |
| 11 | Ironquay | Indemnity limited to the SOW3 payment | Broad IP indemnity; verified payment and confirmatory assignment as the cure |
| 12 | DD-006 incident | "Not material" | Preservation, investigation and update covenants; no assumed breach or figure |
| 13 | Sandbar (AUD 330k) | Ordinary course | Get the documents and assess; no automatic Debt treatment |
| 14 | Tax / IP | "Settled" | Remain open; separate regimes |
| 15 | Title | DD-012 register | Independent ASIC, PPSR, certificate and authority evidence |
| 16 | Lease / Mossvale | Notice only / not triggered | Confirm the readings; add notification to deliverables |

## Next steps

1. **Cover note to the Seller.** State that no clause is agreed, and reject the [STANDARD] categorisation and the asserted acceptance of the disclosure and limitation framework.
2. **Full mark-up.** Reflect the positions above, with the fraud carve-out and the Title regime drafted first.
3. **Leverage.** Use the Seller's own Disclosure Letter as leverage. It contradicts the update on Bluefen ("addressed"), Riverlark, the funds flow ("reflects agreed mechanics"), DD-006 ("not material") and Sandbar ("ordinary course").
4. **Escalation to Amelia Frost.** Raise this only if the team wants authority for the 20% cap, the 18-month period or a post-Completion Riverlark release. Until she gives written authority, none of these is available.
5. **Information requests.** Ask for:
   - the current Bluefen position and the status of the cl 11.3 conditions;
   - a Riverlark payout figure;
   - Ironquay payment evidence;
   - the bonus on-cost calculation;
   - DD-006 investigation material;
   - Sandbar contracts and approvals;
   - independent title searches.

- **Playbook:** fraud, wilful concealment and deliberate misconduct are carved out of all caps, baskets, time limits, exclusive remedies and non-reliance, to the maximum extent enforceable. **No one may waive this.**
- **Why it matters:** As drafted, these provisions would purport to limit claims for the Seller's own fraud. Combined with the non-reliance clause, they would also try to block misrepresentation claims.
- **Push back:** This is non-negotiable. Insert an express carve-out covering fraud, wilful concealment and deliberate misconduct by the Seller, its officers, employees, agents and advisers. It must override every limitation, the exclusive-remedy clause and non-reliance. The team has no authority to concede this point.

### 6. Disclosure (Schedule 7 and Disclosure Letter paras 1.1 and 1.2)

- **What the letter does:** Para 1.1 discloses "every fact, matter and circumstance" in the data room, including DD-002 to DD-012. Para 1.2 adds the Accounts, the statutory registers and "publicly searchable corporate records".
- **Playbook:** require specific fair disclosure, and reject whole-data-room, public-register or prudent-search deemed disclosure.
- **Push back:**
  - Delete 1.1 and 1.2.
  - Only matters fairly disclosed in the letter itself, with enough detail for the Buyer to identify the nature and scope of the matter, should qualify the Warranties.
  - Disclosure must never qualify Title/capacity warranties, specific indemnities or the fraud carve-out.
- **Para 1.4 (non-admission):** A non-admission clause is acceptable in principle. It should be tightened so it cannot be used to argue that a disclosed consent or discharge requirement is "not legally required" and so is not a Completion deliverable.

### 7. Buyer knowledge (cl 8.3): no claim for anything the Buyer or its advisers knew or could discover

- **Playbook:** delete blanket buyer-knowledge exclusions. Any knowledge qualifier must refer to named Seller knowledge persons and reasonable enquiry, and must never excuse title, capacity, fraud or a specific indemnity.
- **Why it matters:** This is a deemed-knowledge bar that reaches our advisers and anything "discoverable". Through the back door, it re-imports the whole-data-room disclosure we are rejecting under item 6. It would also wipe out claims on matters we have specifically identified, such as Ironquay and DD-006.
- **Push back:**
  - Delete cl 8.3.
  - Add an express statement that the Buyer's rights are not affected by any investigation or knowledge, actual, constructive or imputed.
  - Separately, define Seller's knowledge by reference to named individuals who have made reasonable enquiry.

### 8. Bluefen consent (cl 3 / 6.3)

- **The facts:** Bluefen is about AUD 3.6m of FY26 revenue, roughly 30% of the business. Change of control requires consent under cl 11.2, subject to conditions in cl 11.3. The Seller's own letter (para 2) confirms there is **no final consent and no evidence the conditions are satisfied**. The Seller's update calls this "addressed". It is not.
- **The Seller's mechanism falls short of our playbook in two ways:**
  1. "Reasonable endeavours" alone is insufficient for a customer this material.
  2. Treating the condition as satisfied "on delivery of the counterparty's written consent" ignores the cl 11.3 conditions. A consent whose conditions remain unmet may not be effective.
- **Push back:**
  - Make it a condition precedent to Completion, waivable by the Buyer only.
  - The condition is satisfied only by an effective, unconditional (or Buyer-approved) written consent from Bluefen, **plus** evidence satisfactory to the Buyer that every cl 11.3 condition has been met.
  - Strengthen the Seller's obligation beyond reasonable endeavours.
  - Add a pre-Completion information and consultation right for the Buyer.
  - Add a right to terminate if the consent is not obtained by the end date.

### 9. Riverlark facility (cl 2 / 7): release "following Completion"

- **The facts:** About AUD 3.2m is outstanding, with change-of-control (cl 8.1) and discharge (cl 9.2) provisions. The Seller's letter (para 3) confirms the facility is **not repaid and no discharge is included**.
- **Playbook:** require a current payout letter, direct repayment out of Completion funds, and effective security releases at Completion. A post-Completion release needs both an irrevocable undertaking and Amelia Frost's approval. Neither exists.
- **Why it matters:** We are buying debt-free. Change-of-control may trigger default or acceleration. Unreleased security over the Company's assets, or over the shares, would also be a title and encumbrance issue (see item 15).
- **Push back:**
  - Completion deliverables:
    - a current payout letter from Riverlark;
    - payment of the payout amount directly to Riverlark from the Completion funds, deducted from the price;
    - executed deeds of release;
    - PPSR discharges or undertakings to discharge in agreed form.
  - Reject the post-Completion release unless Amelia Frost approves it and it is backed by an irrevocable undertaking.

### 10. Funds flow and the DD-005 bonuses (AUD 420,000)

- **The contradiction:** The Seller says the funds flow "reflects the agreed price mechanics", yet admits the AUD 420k Completion bonuses "are not separately itemised". The letter (para 5) confirms they **do not appear** in the funds flow, and it is silent on payroll tax, superannuation and other on-costs.
- **Why it matters:** These bonuses are triggered by Completion. If the Company pays them after Completion, we bear the cost. "A matter for the Seller" means nothing unless the documents show how the Seller pays for them.
- **Push back:**
  - Either (a) include the bonuses as a specific line item treated as Debt or a transaction expense and deducted from the price, or (b) require the Seller to fund them, with a matching indemnity.
  - In both cases, the bonuses must include all triggered on-costs: payroll tax, superannuation guarantee, PAYG withholding and workers' compensation.
  - The funds flow must state the treatment expressly rather than leave it out.

### 11. Ironquay IP indemnity (cl 11.1): limited to the SOW3 payment

- **The facts:** DD-004 cl 7.3 transfers the SOW3 Project Materials only on cleared payment of every SOW3 fee. DD-010 records AUD 180k as open. The letter (para 4) concedes this is not bank-verified, and there is no payment receipt or confirmatory assignment.
- **Playbook:** broaden the narrow indemnity and preserve the SOW3 cure. The AUD 180k figure is **not independently verified either way**, so we should not assume it is the correct amount owed or that it has been paid.
- **Why it matters:** An indemnity limited to "the SOW3 payment" does not cover the real risk. If ownership of the SOW3 materials has not transferred, the Company may not own IP it uses. That could lead to infringement claims, loss of use, or rework costs well beyond the fee.
- **Push back:**
  - Extend the indemnity to all Losses arising from any failure of the Company to own, or be free to use, the SOW3 Project Materials, and any Ironquay claim relating to them.
  - Keep it outside the general cap, thresholds and disclosure.
  - Preserve the cure: before Completion, the Seller procures (a) verified payment of all outstanding SOW3 fees, at whatever amount is verified, and (b) a confirmatory IP assignment from Ironquay.
  - Ask for bank evidence to settle the AUD 180k question.

### 12. DD-006 export/privacy incident (cl 4.6 / Schedule 6)

- **The facts:** A download link went to an unintended external address. The export may cover about 1,240 records. The Seller's update calls it "preliminary" and "not expected to be material". The letter (para 6) confirms that access, scope and any notification obligation are **unresolved**.
- **Our position:** The Seller's "not material" characterisation should not be accepted. Equally, we should not assert that a breach, harm, notification duty or loss amount exists. Nothing in the record establishes any of these either way, and we should not put a number on it.
- **Push back:**
  - Add pre-Completion covenants requiring the Seller to:
    - preserve all logs and evidence;
    - complete a proper investigation, including whether the incident is an eligible data breach under the *Privacy Act 1988* (Cth) NDB scheme;
    - give the Buyer regular updates and access to findings;
    - consult the Buyer before any notification or regulator contact.
  - The disclosure must not qualify the privacy warranties.
  - Consider a specific indemnity for Losses arising from the incident, sitting outside the general regime. Do not attach a number until the facts are known.

### 13. Sandbar renewals (AUD 330,000 aggregate)

- **The facts:** The Seller says these are "ordinary-course operating costs". Its own letter (para 8) says it does **not** state whether each renewal is unavoidable, terminable, accrued or in the ordinary course. It also says DD-008 and DD-011 should be "read together for timing/scope". Three "related" renewals of exactly AUD 110k each is worth looking at, for example whether a single commitment was split below an approval threshold.
- **Playbook:** assess the renewals. Do not classify them automatically as Debt or deduct them from the price.
- **Push back:** Do not accept the "ordinary course" label without evidence. Ask for:
  - the contracts;
  - approval records;
  - terms on termination and payment;
  - accrual treatment.

  Reserve our position on warranty or price treatment until we have assessed these. Do not demand a price deduction at this stage.

### 14. Tax and IP: Seller says "settled under the general regime"

- **Playbook:** Tax and IP terms remain **OPEN**. They are not resolved, and we should assume no unlimited liability in either direction.
- **Push back:** Record that Tax and IP are open and will have their own separate regimes. They must not default into the general cap, thresholds or time limits, whether through the item 3 override or through this statement.

### 15. Title: Seller relies on the DD-012 share register

- **The issue:** DD-012 is the Company's own internal register, supplied by the Seller. The letter (para 10) itself concedes it is not independent verification.
- **Push back:** Require independent evidence of title, ownership, encumbrances and authority, including:
  - current ASIC company extracts showing members;
  - original or replacement share certificates;
  - a PPSR search over the Seller and the Company, with any security over the shares released at Completion (see item 9);
  - Seller board resolutions and evidence of authority;
  - executed share transfer forms.

  The Title warranties stay in the separate fundamental regime (item 4) and are not qualified by disclosure or buyer knowledge.

### 16. Lower-priority items: office lease (DD-007) and Mossvale (DD-009)

- The letter indicates a notification obligation under the lease and an assignment restriction under Mossvale that does not appear to be triggered by a share sale. Neither looks like a consent requirement on the material provided.
- **Action:** Have our counsel confirm both readings, including whether either document has a change-of-control clause. Add the lease notification to Completion deliverables or post-Completion covenants. These are low priority but should be closed out.
